newsitem.title: USA: Pop star Jackson marries woman carrying his child.
newsitem.headline: Pop star Jackson marries woman carrying his child.

text.p: Pop superstar Michael Jackson married the woman who is carrying his child in an early morning ceremony held in Sydney, Australia, his publicist said on Thursday.

Christine Holevas, Jackson's spokeswoman, said the singer exchanged wedding vows with Debbie Rowe, a 37-year-old nurse, while on the Australian leg of his HIStory world tour. "They are married. All I know is that it happened," Holevas said.
"Please respect our privacy and let us enjoy this wonderful and exciting time," Jackson told reporters in a written statement.
The wedding took place only 10 days after Jackson announced that Rowe, a longtime friend, was pregnant and was due to give birth in early 1997.
Jackson denied news reports that Rowe had been artificially inseminated and had been paid to carry his child. But at the time there was no mention of wedding plans.

This is Jackson's second marriage. In January, Lisa Marie Presley, daughter of late rock-and-roll legend Elvis Presley, filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences, 20 months after they were married in a secret ceremony in the Dominican Republic.

Some Hollywood insiders had speculated that Jackson's first marriage was little more than a publicity stunt to deflect media attention that had mushroomed around claims that Jackson sexually molested a young boy. Jackson had vehemently denied the boy's allegations.

Rowe reportedly has been divorced for eight years from her first husband and lives in an apartment in the Los Angeles suburb of Van Nuys. She is said to have met Jackson 15 years ago while working for a doctor who was treating the entertainer for a rare skin condition.
Jackson was in Australia on Thursday on the first leg of his HIStory world tour to promote his latest album, a compilation of new songs and some of his best known hits.

Jackson's tour of Asia in October sparked controversy wherever it went. In Malaysia one concert was abruptly cancelled by local authorities over concerns the show could have undesirable effects on youth.

Attempts by civic and religious groups in South Korea to have a concert banned failed when the Ministry of Culture said Jackson could perform provided he refrained from making "obscene or vulgar gestures and remarks."
